findings.title: die_model='distributed' decks are rejected by FastHenry (nodes used before they are defined)
findings.detail: In the distributed branch, the loop over sorted footprint cells writes node Nd..k, its column, and then the lateral segments Edx/Edy to the neighbour (k+1). The neighbour node is only written in a later loop iteration. FastHenry 3.0wr reads the deck in order, so every lateral die-top segment fails with 'No node read in yet named nd...', and it exits with code 1 without writing Zc.mat. The F6 die variant, half of the claimed 'F6 model variants', therefore cannot produce any result. The tab variant and the default models do run.
findings.evidence: Exported 2D_Case_2R with FHLevel() and die_model='distributed' (terminal 'point' and 'tab'), then ran ~/.local/bin/fasthenry deck.inp -s ludecomp -m direct. Both runs exited 1 with 152 'No node read in yet' errors (4 dies x 38 lateral segments). Example: deck line 3941 'Edx0i13y16 Nd0i13y16 Nd0i14y16 ...' comes before line 3962 'Nd0i14y16 x=...'. The short/point and short/tab decks from the same layout exited 0 with valid Zc.mat files.
findings.suggested_check: Write all die-top nodes of a group before its Ev/Ed segments, and add a test that every segment, .equiv and .external node is defined on an earlier line (or run FastHenry once on a small deck).

findings.title: The F6 well-formedness test cannot catch an invalid deck
findings.detail: test_f6_variants_are_well_formed_together checks only that each node referenced by a segment, .equiv or .external exists somewhere in the parsed deck (a dict). It ignores the order in which FastHenry requires nodes to be defined. So it passes a distributed deck that FastHenry refuses. No test runs FastHenry or checks definition order, so the tests do not support the claim that the F6 variants are correctly implemented.
findings.evidence: The test passes (24 passed), yet the same kind of deck fails in FastHenry (finding 1).
findings.suggested_check: Assert that each referenced node's first definition comes before its first use.

findings.title: Lateral die-block segments are centred on the die-top surface, so half the block lies above the die
findings.detail: The die-top nodes sit at z = DieShort.z_top, and the lateral Ed segments use h = z_top - z_bottom (0.23 mm). FastHenry centres a segment's cross-section on its node line, so the lateral conductor spans z_top ± 0.115 mm. Half of it is above the die top, rather than inside the attach + die block the docstring describes. The docstring mentions the volume being counted twice but not this offset. The effect on the F6 ratio diagnostic is likely small against its 2 % threshold.
findings.evidence: 2R deck: 'Nd0i13y16 ... z=0.002466', 'Edx0i13y16 ... h=0.00023'. The stack puts the block from 2.236 to 2.466 mm.
findings.suggested_check: Put the lateral die nodes at the block mid-height, or state the offset in the docstring.

findings.title: Contact ties short a few trace segments, while die-footprint segments are dropped for the same reason
findings.detail: When a wire foot or port lies on a cell edge or corner, the tied cells are merged by .equiv, but the lattice segments between them are kept. These become exactly the self-loops the docstring gives as the reason for dropping die-group segments. FastHenry tolerates them (P4 ran Case 4 at 0.5 mm with 8 of them), so the only cost is an inconsistency and a small spurious eddy current.
findings.evidence: Self-loop counts in short/point: Case 4 and 2R at 0.5 and 0.25 mm: 8 each; 2D_Case_6 at 0.5 mm: 16, at 0.25 mm: 40 (all 8 wire feet tie 4 ways); distributed/point at 0.25 mm: 72.
findings.suggested_check: Drop segments whose two ends are in the same .equiv class, or document that they are kept.

findings.title: Plane-pitch test assertion is weakened by an 'or'
findings.detail: test_plane_pitch_is_separate_from_trace_pitch accepts (seg1, seg2) when abs(seg1 - 2*seg1_4mm) <= 1 regardless of seg2. Only the hard-coded 40 x 55 baseplate check constrains seg2.
findings.suggested_check: Assert each of seg1 and seg2 separately against round(extent / pitch).

findings.title: With the default conductivity the distributed die is a solid copper block
findings.detail: die_sigma defaults to the top-Cu conductivity, giving a 0.23 mm copper block. That conducts sideways far better than a real die (vertical device with a thin source metallisation), so the F6 diagnostic may understate how far the ideal-short assumption is from reality. The docstring states this choice and die_sigma can be overridden.
findings.evidence: fasthenry.py: sig_d = sigma_top if die_sigma is None else die_sigma.
findings.suggested_check: Report F6 die results for at least one lower die_sigma as a sensitivity check.

independent_checks_performed: Ran uv run pytest -q tests/unit/test_fasthenry.py (24 passed) and the ruff check on both files (clean).
Diffed the module against research/scripts/o006_p4/fh_export.py: the default-model code is unchanged apart from the origin, validation and the new variants.

Exported the judged references 2D_Case_2R and 2D_Case_6 (o003_powersynth_references.build) for every die_model x terminal_model combination at 1.0, 0.5 and 0.25 mm: all export without error, die groups have 24/96/384 cells, and tab footprints have 9/36/144 cells (9 mm^2 at every pitch).
Built the .equiv equivalence classes with a union-find and counted segments with both ends in one class (self-loops) per variant and level.

Ran the local FastHenry 3.0wr (direct LU) on 2R coarse decks: short/point gives Z = 0.00413 + 1.05152j at 10 MHz (16.735 nH, same L at 20 MHz); short/tab runs; both distributed decks exit 1 with 152 'No node read in yet' errors.

Physics check of the tab model by post height: 10 um -> 15.746 nH, 2 mm -> 16.731 nH, 10 mm -> 22.820 nH. L rises monotonically with height. The 10 mm posts add 7.07 nH against about 7.4 nH from the closed-form partial self-inductance of a 3x3 mm bar, L = (mu0 l / 2 pi)[ln(2l/(w+t)) + 1/2 + 0.2235 (w+t)/l] (Rosa/Grover), times two posts.

Checked the deck geometry by hand against the stack: plane mid-plane z values, trace mid-thickness nodes, column and post z-ranges, equal-GMD wire side 0.8711 d (0.7788 r / 0.44705), and the ndec value that gives exactly the 10 and 20 MHz points.
caveats: FastHenry was run only at the coarse level (1 mm cell, 4 mm planes, nh=1) with the direct solver. Finer levels and the multipole solver were not run, and absolute L was not compared with l2_layout.
The FastHenry warning 'DivideSegs: tried to divide an indivisable segment' also appears in the default deck and was not investigated.
The tab variant and the default models are sound as far as checked. The reject rests on the distributed-die variant alone.
